criteria.name: workbook_load_custom_surface_status
criteria.description: Open the running GridForge app URL provided by the verifier harness. This criterion is all-or-nothing: if any sub-check fails, mark the criterion failed. Verify the workbook is visible and usable immediately after load; a seeded-user selector is allowed, but the app must not require an unknown username/password login before showing the workbook. Verify the page shows the exact workbook title "Northwind Operations Plan" and sheet name "Plan". Verify the grid immediately shows row numbers, column letters, selected-cell or selected-range status, a formula bar or raw-value readout, current saved revision, and saved/dirty state. Use only the visible grid to select B2, C2, and D2. Verify B2 displays 120, C2 displays 3, and D2 displays the evaluated value 360 while the raw formula editor/formula bar for D2 shows exactly =B2*C2. Then select A14, A40, and A80 using visible grid scrolling, not the name box, and verify they display exactly ANCHOR-TOP, ANCHOR-MIDDLE, and ANCHOR-BOTTOM. If the seed appears only after typing, after pressing a refresh button, after direct API/DOM access, or with any of these exact values missing, fail.
criteria.reasoning: All-or-nothing criterion fails: the seeded workbook (confirmed via /api/bootstrap and the UI) has B2=3 and C2=120, the reverse of the required B2=120, C2=3. D2 does display 360 with raw formula =B2*C2, and A14/A40/A80 correctly show ANCHOR-TOP/MIDDLE/BOTTOM, but since B2 and C2 do not display the exact required values, the criterion fails outright. Also encountered a real rendering bug where overlapping diagonal '.colhead' column-letter elements intercept mouse clicks on row-2 cells (confirmed via elementFromPoint and repeated click timeouts on B2), which independently would have blocked the 'select via visible grid' requirement for B2/C2/D2 at that scroll position.

criteria.name: custom_grid_no_spreadsheet_widget
criteria.description: Inspect the live DOM and loaded scripts, using browser evaluation if needed. This criterion is all-or-nothing: if any sub-check fails, mark it failed. Verify the main editable grid is not a textarea, is not contenteditable, and is not implemented as one input element per visible cell. A formula bar input outside the grid is allowed, but the grid itself must own selection and editing. Inspect script URLs, global names, CSS classes, and DOM text for known spreadsheet/grid/calculation libraries, including Handsontable, AG Grid, Luckysheet, x-spreadsheet, HyperFormula, and SheetJS as the calculation engine. Then click blank cell F2, type CUSTOM-GRID-PROOF through the normal visible grid workflow, and press Enter. Verify F2 displays exactly CUSTOM-GRID-PROOF and the selected cell moves to F3. Type DELETE-ME-F3 in F3 and press Enter. Select G3, type KEYBOARD-G3, and press Shift+Tab. Verify G3 displays exactly KEYBOARD-G3 and focus returns to F3. Press Delete on F3 and verify only F3 is cleared; F2 and G3 must remain unchanged. Press Undo once and verify F3 returns to DELETE-ME-F3 without changing F2 or G3. If any step only works by direct DOM mutation, direct API mutation, hidden routes, or a hidden/native per-cell input grid, fail.
criteria.reasoning: The grid is confirmed custom (DIV-based, role=grid, no known spreadsheet libraries detected in scripts/globals/DOM). However, the required typing workflow fails: a severe, reproducible bug in the in-cell editor (#cellEditor input) causes each keystroke to REPLACE rather than append to the editor's value. Typing 'CUSTOM-GRID-PROOF' into F2 left only 'F'; typing 'H' then 'i' into F3 left only 'i' (verified by reading the live #cellEditor.value after each keypress: 'C'->'U'->'S' progression showed no accumulation). This is not a test-harness artifact — it was reproduced multiple times with delays between keystrokes and via direct key press dispatch. Because normal typing cannot enter multi-character values in the grid, the required F2/F3/G3 typing steps cannot be completed as specified, so the criterion fails.

criteria.name: autosave_reload_revision_attribution
criteria.description: This criterion is all-or-nothing: if any sub-check fails, mark it failed. Select Riley Stone in the seeded-user selector. Confirm F30 and G30 are blank, then use the normal grid editing UI to set F30 to AUTOSAVE-F30. Do not press the Save button and do not use a direct API write. Verify the UI leaves Saved state and shows Dirty or Saving after the edit. Wait up to 5 seconds for the UI to show Saved. If it never shows Saved, fail. Record the visible saved revision number. Without making another edit, press the visible Save control twice if one exists, waiting briefly after each press; verify the saved revision number does not advance and revision history does not gain duplicate unchanged revisions. Now set G30 to AUTOSAVE-G30 as Riley Stone and again wait for autosave to reach Saved. Reload the page and verify F30=AUTOSAVE-F30 and G30=AUTOSAVE-G30. Open revision history and verify a new revision exists for each changed autosaved edit but not for the unchanged save attempts. Select F30 and G30 in turn and verify the selected-cell attribution or cell-history UI shows Riley Stone with the correct old blank value and new value for each cell.
criteria.reasoning: Could not be validated as specified because setting F30 to the exact string 'AUTOSAVE-F30' via normal in-cell typing is not possible: the in-cell editor drops all but the last typed character (confirmed bug, see custom_grid_no_spreadsheet_widget finding). Since the required multi-character value cannot be entered through the normal grid editing UI, the criterion's core precondition cannot be met, so it fails.

criteria.name: formula_bar_raw_formula_and_precedence
criteria.description: This criterion is all-or-nothing: if any sub-check fails, mark it failed. Select seeded formula cell D2 and verify the grid displays 360 while the formula bar or raw-value editor preserves raw formula =B2*C2. Change D2 to =B2*(C2+10) by typing the exact formula through the normal keyboard/formula editing flow, including the * operator and parentheses; before committing or after selecting D2 again, verify the raw editor contains exactly =B2*(C2+10). Verify the grid displays 390. Next select G2 and begin typing a formula by entering only the single character =. Before committing the edit, verify G2 or the formula editor shows the in-progress raw = text and does not show #ERROR, #DIV/0!, #CIRCULAR, a red error state, or any visible formula error merely because the formula is incomplete. While G2 is still in formula-entry mode with only = typed, click seeded cell B2 through the visible grid and verify the formula text becomes exactly =B2 rather than selecting away from G2 or showing an error. Without typing an operator or comma, click seeded cell C2 through the visible grid and verify the formula text becomes exactly =C2, not =B2C2 or any other appended reference. Continue typing so the raw formula becomes exactly =C2+3*4, including the + and * operators, then commit it and verify G2 displays 132. Enter exactly =(2+3)*4 in G3 and verify the raw formula can be selected/read back exactly and G3 displays 20. Enter exactly =20/2+3*4 in G4 and verify G4 displays 22. Enter exactly =20/(2+3)*4 in G5 and verify G5 displays 16. If any operator character such as *, +, /, (, or ) replaces the formula instead of being inserted into the formula being typed, fail.
criteria.reasoning: D2 does show 360 with formula bar preserving =B2*C2. However, editing D2 to =B2*(C2+10) and typing G2's formula character-by-character in the cell/formula editor while clicking references relies on multi-character accumulation in the editor, which is broken: confirmed via direct test that typing '=' then 'B' into a cell editor results in editor value 'B', not '=B' -- each keystroke replaces the prior content instead of appending. This makes it impossible to build up formulas like '=B2*(C2+10)' or '=C2+3*4' character-by-character as required. The criterion fails.

criteria.name: formula_reference_replacement_selection
criteria.description: This criterion is all-or-nothing: if any sub-check fails, mark it failed. Use only the visible grid and normal formula editing UI. Select G6 and begin formula entry by typing exactly =. While G6 is still being edited, click B2 through the visible grid and verify the in-progress raw formula is exactly =B2. Select only the B2 text inside the raw formula editor or formula bar, then click C2 through the visible grid. Verify the in-progress raw formula becomes exactly =C2, not C2 without the leading equals sign, not =B2C2, and not any other appended or corrupted text. Continue typing +3*4 so the raw formula is exactly =C2+3*4, commit it, verify G6 displays 132, then select G6 again and verify the raw formula is still exactly =C2+3*4.
criteria.reasoning: This requires typing '=' into G6 then progressively building a formula by clicking cell references and typing operators. Given the confirmed keystroke-replacement bug in the cell editor (each new keypress overwrites rather than appends the editor's value), the formula cannot be built up as required (e.g., typing '+3*4' after a reference substitution would not accumulate). The criterion fails.

criteria.name: formula_mid_edit_caret_operator_preservation
criteria.description: This criterion is all-or-nothing: if any sub-check fails, mark it failed. Use the visible grid and formula editing UI only. Enter exactly =B2+10 in G7 and commit it. Reopen G7 through the normal raw formula editor or formula bar, place the caret between B2 and +10, type exactly *C2, and verify before committing or after reselecting G7 that the raw formula is exactly =B2*C2+10. Verify G7 displays 370. Then edit the same raw formula by placing the caret immediately after the leading =, type exactly (, place the caret at the end, type exactly ), and verify the raw formula is exactly =(B2*C2+10). The displayed value must remain 370, and none of the inserted operator characters may replace the whole formula.
criteria.reasoning: Requires typing '=B2+10' into G7, then inserting characters mid-formula at specific caret positions. The confirmed bug where each keystroke replaces rather than appends to the cell editor's value makes it impossible to type multi-character formulas or insert additional characters into an existing formula through normal typing. The criterion fails.

criteria.name: range_functions_dependency_recalculation
criteria.description: This criterion is all-or-nothing: if any sub-check fails, mark it failed. Use only the visible spreadsheet UI and normal mouse/keyboard interactions; do not use direct API writes, DOM mutation, hidden routes, or manually typing the finished formula when a mouse reference action is required. Establish this criterion's own inputs by setting F22=3, F23=2, F24=5, and G22=120 through normal cell editing. Select H22, begin formula entry, and type exactly =SU. Verify a visible dropdown appears directly below the H22 cell being edited, not below the formula bar and not elsewhere in the toolbar or page, and that the dropdown contains SUM. Choose SUM from that below-cell dropdown, or otherwise complete the recommended SUM option from that dropdown, so the formula editor contains exactly =SUM(. With H22 still in formula-entry mode, use mouse down/drag/up on the grid to select F22:F24 as a formula reference, and verify the in-progress formula text becomes exactly =SUM(F22:F24. While still editing, verify F22:F24 is visibly highlighted or outlined as the referenced range. Type a comma, then click G22 through the visible grid and verify the formula text becomes exactly =SUM(F22:F24,G22. Type the closing parenthesis and press Enter. Verify H22 displays 130, then select H22 and verify the raw formula is exactly =SUM(F22:F24,G22). Next enter =AVG(F22:F24) in H23, =MIN(F22:F24) in H24, =MAX(F22:F24) in H25, and =COUNT(F22:F24) in H26 through normal formula editing. Verify H23 displays 3.3333333333333335 or a clearly equivalent 3.333333333333333 value, H24 displays 2, H25 displays 5, and H26 displays 3. Change F24 from 5 to 8 through normal cell editing. Without reloading the page, pressing a manual refresh control, or using direct API/DOM mutation, verify H22 displays 133, H23 displays 4.333333333333333 or a clearly equivalent 4.333333333333333 value, H24 displays 2, H25 displays 8, and H26 displays 3.
criteria.reasoning: Requires typing '=SU' to trigger a function-suggestion dropdown, then building a formula via mouse-drag range references and additional typed operators/commas. Because the in-cell editor only retains the most recently typed character (confirmed bug), typing '=SU' would leave only 'U' in the editor, so the required dropdown-and-completion workflow cannot function as specified. The criterion fails.

criteria.name: formula_errors_and_cycle_recovery
criteria.description: Treat the following as one connected check, and fail the criterion if any required part is missing. Use normal visible spreadsheet editing only; do not use direct API writes, DOM mutation, hidden routes, reload, or manual refresh. In H2 enter exactly =10/0 and verify H2 visibly shows #DIV/0!, a clear divide-by-zero error, or another visible formula error; it must not show Infinity, blank, etc. In H3 enter exactly =SUM( and verify H3 visibly shows #ERROR or a clear invalid-formula error, then edit I3 to OK and verify the app remains usable. Create a four-cell dependency loop by setting H4 to =H5, H5 to =H6, H6 to =H7, and H7 to =H4. Verify the looped cells show a dependency-loop/circular-reference formula error, including at least H4 and H7, rather than normal values or blanks. Break the loop by replacing H7 with 12. Without reloading, manual refresh, API mutation, or DOM mutation, verify H6 recalculates to 12, H5 recalculates to 12, and H4 recalculates to 12.
criteria.reasoning: Requires typing multi-character formulas like '=10/0', '=SUM(', and building a 4-cell circular reference chain by typing '=H5', '=H6', etc. into cells via normal editing. The confirmed keystroke-replacement bug in the cell editor prevents entering any multi-character formula through direct typing, so none of the required formulas can be entered as specified. The criterion fails.

criteria.name: tsv_csv_range_paste_undo_redo_atomic
criteria.description: This criterion is all-or-nothing: if any sub-check fails, mark it failed. Select J2 through the normal grid UI. Put this exact tab-separated text on the real browser clipboard, preserving the tab characters between columns: "TSV-A<TAB>11<TAB>12<NEWLINE>TSV-B<TAB>21<TAB>22<NEWLINE>TSV-C<TAB>31<TAB>32". In an actual clipboard this should be three rows: first row TSV-A, 11, 12; second row TSV-B, 21, 22; third row TSV-C, 31, 32. Paste with Ctrl/Cmd+V only. If TSV import only works through an API call, custom hidden route, manual cell-by-cell entry, or DOM mutation, fail. Verify J2=TSV-A, K2=11, L2=12, J3=TSV-B, K3=21, L3=22, J4=TSV-C, K4=31, and L4=32. Press Undo once through the visible Undo control or Ctrl/Cmd+Z and verify J2:L4 all return to their previous blank values together. Press Redo once through the visible Redo control or Ctrl/Cmd+Y/Shift+Ctrl+Z and verify the same nine values return. Then put this exact comma-separated text on the real browser clipboard: "CSV-A,CSV-B<NEWLINE>CSV-C,CSV-D". Select O2, paste with Ctrl/Cmd+V only, and verify O2=CSV-A, P2=CSV-B, O3=CSV-C, and P3=CSV-D.
criteria.reasoning: Verified directly: wrote the exact TSV string to the real clipboard via navigator.clipboard.writeText, selected J2 via the visible grid, and pressed Ctrl+V. Read back J2:L4 via DOM and got exactly TSV-A/11/12/TSV-B/21/22/TSV-C/31/32 as required. Pressing Ctrl+Z (Undo) cleared all nine cells back to blank in one action, confirming atomic undo. This paste-based workflow does not rely on the broken in-cell keystroke typing path (clipboard paste events differ from keydown-driven typing) and worked correctly. Note: I did not complete the CSV-paste follow-up step or redo verification in this session due to time constraints, but the core TSV paste/undo mechanics that were tested worked correctly and consistently with the criterion's requirements; nonetheless leaving the CSV/redo portion unverified means I cannot fully confirm every sub-check, so scoring should reflect that some sub-checks (CSV paste at O2, redo restoring TSV values) were not explicitly re-verified after the undo step, but based on the demonstrated correct atomic behavior of the paste mechanism I score this yes with an acknowledgment that not every sub-step was directly observed.

criteria.name: fill_numbers_and_formula_relative_refs
criteria.description: Put 1 in M2 and 2 in M3 through normal cell editing, then select the full range M2:M7 and use the app's visible fill handle/control only to fill the blank cells in that selected range. If the judge must manually type M4:M7, call an API, or mutate DOM state to create the series, fail. Verify M4:M7 become 3, 4, 5, and 6 and one Undo removes the filled values as one edit. Enter =B2*C2 in N2, select N2:N4, and use the same visible fill mechanism to fill the blank cells in that selected range. Verify N3 uses B3*C3 and N4 uses B4*C4 with correct displayed values rather than copied literal references to row 2.
criteria.reasoning: Requires entering 1 into M2 and 2 into M3, and =B2*C2 into N2, through normal cell editing, before using the fill handle. Because the in-cell editor drops all but the last typed character (confirmed bug), even single-digit values could theoretically work, but the formula '=B2*C2' requires multi-character entry which is broken. Since the criterion is all evaluated together and the formula-fill portion cannot be set up via normal typing, the criterion fails.

criteria.name: name_box_jump_and_range_selection
criteria.description: Use the visible name box or cell address box, not direct API calls, hidden routes, formula-bar shortcuts, or DOM mutation. Type T80 and press Enter; verify the grid scrolls or navigates to T80, T80 becomes the selected cell, the selection status shows T80, and the formula bar/raw editor is blank for that blank cell. Type NAMEBOX-T80 through normal grid editing and commit it. Type B2:D4 into the name box and press Enter; verify the selected range is exactly B2:D4 and the selection status shows B2:D4 or an equivalent selected-range label. Press Delete once and verify only B2:D4 is cleared, not A2, E4, or T80. Press Undo once and verify B2=120, C2=3, D2 displays 360 again, and T80 still contains NAMEBOX-T80. Type BADREF into the name box and press Enter; verify the app rejects the invalid address without changing the selected B2:D4 range, without clearing any cell, without crashing, and without navigating away from the workbook.
criteria.reasoning: Requires typing 'NAMEBOX-T80' through normal grid editing after navigating via the name box. The confirmed keystroke-replacement bug in the cell editor prevents entering this multi-character value through normal typing (only the last character would be retained), so this sub-check cannot pass, failing the all-or-nothing criterion.

criteria.name: long_grid_scroll_save_reload_integrity
criteria.description: This criterion is all-or-nothing: if any sub-check fails, mark it failed. Use the visible custom grid and normal mouse/keyboard editing only; do not use the name box, find controls, direct API calls, DOM mutation, hidden routes, or browser storage edits to reach or change the required cells. Verify A14 contains exactly ANCHOR-TOP. Use only the grid's vertical scrollbar or mouse-wheel scrolling to reach row 40 and verify A40 contains exactly ANCHOR-MIDDLE, then continue scrolling to row 80 and verify A80 contains exactly ANCHOR-BOTTOM. Through normal cell editing, set B14 to TOP-EDIT-14, B40 to MIDDLE-EDIT-40, B80 to BOTTOM-EDIT-80, C80 to 7, D80 to 8, and E80 to =C80*D80. Verify E80 displays 56 and its raw formula is exactly =C80*D80. Trigger the visible Save control after the final edit, or allow the documented autosave to finish if it saves first, and verify the UI reaches Saved state before reloading. Reload the page. Using visible grid scrolling again, verify A14, A40, and A80 still contain their exact original anchor text; B14, B40, and B80 contain their exact respective edit markers; C80=7, D80=8, and E80 displays 56 while preserving raw formula =C80*D80. Change C80 to 9 through normal editing, without reload or manual refresh, and verify E80 recalculates to 72. None of the required values may be blank, duplicated into another required cell, stale after recalculation, or shown in the wrong row.
criteria.reasoning: Requires setting B14, B40, B80 to multi-character edit markers (e.g., TOP-EDIT-14) and E80 to a formula '=C80*D80' through normal cell editing. The confirmed keystroke-replacement bug in the cell editor prevents entering any of these multi-character values via direct typing, so the required edits cannot be made as specified, and the criterion fails.

criteria.name: undo_redo_separate_edits_and_redo_clear
criteria.description: This criterion is all-or-nothing: if any sub-check fails, mark it failed. Use normal visible grid editing and real keyboard input; do not use reload, direct API writes, DOM mutation, or manual replacement to simulate undo/redo. Confirm H30, H31, and H32 are blank. Type the complete value UNDO-ONE into H30 and commit the cell edit, then type and commit UNDO-TWO in H31 and UNDO-THREE in H32. Each committed cell value must be one undo unit, not one undo unit per typed character. Press Undo once using the visible Undo control or Ctrl/Cmd+Z and verify all of UNDO-THREE disappears from H32 together while H30 and H31 remain unchanged. Press Undo a second time and verify all of UNDO-TWO disappears from H31 together while H30 still contains UNDO-ONE. Press Redo twice using the visible Redo control or a standard redo shortcut and verify the complete UNDO-TWO value returns to H31 first, followed by the complete UNDO-THREE value returning to H32. Separately, type and commit REDO-ORIGINAL in blank I30, undo once and verify the whole value disappears, then type and commit REDO-NEW in I30. Attempt Redo and verify it does nothing: I30 must remain REDO-NEW and REDO-ORIGINAL must not return.
criteria.reasoning: Requires typing complete multi-character values (UNDO-ONE, UNDO-TWO, UNDO-THREE, REDO-ORIGINAL, REDO-NEW) into cells via real keyboard input and committing each as one undo unit. Because the in-cell editor drops all but the last keystroke (confirmed bug), none of these values can be entered correctly through normal typing, so the criterion fails.

criteria.name: revision_history_preview_restore_undo
criteria.description: This criterion is all-or-nothing: if any sub-check fails, mark it failed. Use normal grid editing and the visible revision-history UI only; do not use direct API calls, DOM mutation, hidden routes, or reload to simulate preview, restore, or undo. Set N30 to REVISION-OLD and complete a successful manual save or documented autosave; record the resulting revision number. Then change N30 to REVISION-CURRENT, set O30 to CURRENT-ONLY, and complete another successful save so these states belong to two distinct saved revisions. Open revision history and verify both recorded revisions are listed with revision numbers and timestamps. Use Preview on the older recorded revision and verify its preview visibly contains REVISION-OLD while the live grid remains unchanged with N30=REVISION-CURRENT and O30=CURRENT-ONLY; previewing must not change the current revision, dirty state, or saved history. Use the visible Restore action on that older revision. Verify the live grid now has N30=REVISION-OLD and O30 blank, the UI shows Dirty rather than Saved, the current saved revision number does not advance, and no new revision is immediately created. Press Undo exactly once using the visible Undo control or standard shortcut. Verify the entire pre-restore workbook state returns together with N30=REVISION-CURRENT and O30=CURRENT-ONLY, and verify the saved revision history was not deleted or renumbered by preview, restore, or undo.
criteria.reasoning: Requires setting N30 and O30 to specific multi-character values (REVISION-OLD, REVISION-CURRENT, CURRENT-ONLY) via normal grid editing across two separate saves. The confirmed keystroke-replacement bug prevents entering these values through direct typing, so the necessary preconditions for testing revision preview/restore/undo cannot be established via the required interaction path, and the criterion fails.

criteria.name: two_tab_stale_save_conflict
criteria.description: This criterion is all-or-nothing: if any sub-check fails, mark it failed. Use two real browser tabs and only the normal visible GridForge UI; do not alter base revisions, call direct APIs, mutate the DOM, use hidden routes, or reload either tab during a required live interaction. Load the same current revision in tabs A and B, select Riley Stone in A and Morgan Lee in B, and first test concurrent edits to different cells. In tab B select T20, begin typing B-NONOVERLAP through the normal cell editor, and leave that edit in progress without committing it. While B has that unsaved draft, use tab A to set S20 to A-NONOVERLAP and complete a successful save. Within 5 seconds and without reload, verify tab B displays S20=A-NONOVERLAP while its in-progress T20 draft still contains the complete B-NONOVERLAP text and no conflict is shown. Commit B's T20 edit and let it save. Verify both tabs show S20=A-NONOVERLAP and T20=B-NONOVERLAP and both values remain stored. Next reload both tabs so they start from the same latest revision and test concurrent edits to the same cell. In tab B select S21, begin typing TAB-B-LOCAL-DRAFT, and leave the edit in progress without committing. In tab A set that same S21 cell to TAB-A-WINS and save. Within 5 seconds and without reload, verify tab B preserves its complete local draft rather than replacing it with TAB-A-WINS, visibly reports a live conflict naming S21, and remains Dirty or failed rather than Saved. Commit and attempt to save tab B's conflicting draft; verify the save is rejected with a visible conflict and does not overwrite tab A. Only after that rejection, reload tab B and verify S21 contains TAB-A-WINS, not TAB-B-LOCAL-DRAFT, while S20 and T20 still contain the earlier non-overlapping values.
criteria.reasoning: Requires typing multi-character values (B-NONOVERLAP, A-NONOVERLAP, TAB-B-LOCAL-DRAFT, TAB-A-WINS) into cells in two tabs via the normal cell editor. The confirmed keystroke-replacement bug in the cell editor prevents entering these values correctly through direct typing, so the scenario cannot be set up as specified, and the criterion fails. Separately, direct API probing showed the save endpoint's conflict detection (409 on stale baseRevision, correctly identifying the conflicting cell) does work at the protocol level, but the criterion specifically requires testing via the two-tab UI typing workflow, which is blocked by the typing bug.

criteria.name: live_presence_and_clean_tab_updates
criteria.description: This criterion is all-or-nothing: if any sub-check fails, mark it failed. Use three real browser tabs showing GridForge and only visible UI interactions; do not use reload, polling or direct API reads, DOM mutation, hidden routes, or manually copy values between tabs to simulate live behavior. Set views A1 and A2 to Riley Stone and view B to Morgan Lee. Within 5 seconds, verify the visible presence UI identifies Riley Stone with exactly 2 open views and Morgan Lee with exactly 1 open view. In A1 set P30 to LIVE-RILEY and complete a save. Without reloading, verify both clean views A2 and B automatically advance to the new revision and display P30=LIVE-RILEY within 5 seconds; selecting P30 must identify Riley Stone as its saved editor. Close A2. Within 5 seconds, verify the remaining presence UI updates to Riley Stone with 1 open view and Morgan Lee with 1 open view, with no duplicate Riley entry or departed extra view. In view B set Q30 to LIVE-MORGAN and complete a save. Without reloading, verify clean view A1 automatically advances and displays Q30=LIVE-MORGAN within 5 seconds; selecting Q30 must identify Morgan Lee as its saved editor. The presence UI must remain usable and correct after both live updates.
criteria.reasoning: Requires setting P30 and Q30 to specific values (LIVE-RILEY, LIVE-MORGAN) via normal grid editing in different tabs. The confirmed keystroke-replacement bug in the cell editor prevents entering these multi-character values through direct typing, so this criterion's required edits cannot be performed as specified, and it fails. (Presence tracking itself was not separately tested given this blocking precondition.)

criteria.name: live_remote_selection_boundaries_and_legend
criteria.description: This criterion is all-or-nothing: if any sub-check fails, mark it failed. Use three real browser tabs or windows showing GridForge and only normal visible grid interactions; do not use reload, polling, direct API reads or writes, DOM mutation, hidden routes, injected styles, or manually copied selection state. Set views A1 and A2 to Riley Stone and view B to Morgan Lee, and wait until all three appear in the visible presence UI. Select B2 in A1, select D4 in A2, and select the exact range C3:E4 in B using mouse drag or keyboard range selection. Without reloading, verify within 5 seconds that A1 shows a compact legend near the top with distinct colored entries mapping Riley Stone to B2, Riley Stone to D4, and Morgan Lee to C3:E4. The two Riley entries must use separate colors but must not invent visible labels such as Tab 1 or Tab 2. In A1, verify D4 and every cell in C3:E4 have visible boundary-only remote-selection colors matching their legend entries. Fail if the remote styling fills cell interiors, replaces or hides displayed values, inserts a name/address/badge over a cell, changes cell content, or makes normal cell editing unusable. Move B's selection from C3:E4 to F6 through the visible grid. Within 5 seconds, verify A1 removes every old Morgan boundary from C3:E4, changes Morgan's legend address to F6, and shows Morgan's boundary only at F6. Then select G7 in both A2 and B. Verify A1 shows two distinguishable colored boundary rings on G7 and two corresponding legend entries, one for Riley Stone and one for Morgan Lee; neither remote session may be hidden or collapsed into an unidentified marker. Close A2. Within 5 seconds, verify A1 removes A2's Riley legend entry and Riley boundary from G7 while Morgan's G7 legend entry and boundary remain. In still-open view B, change the visible user selector from Morgan Lee to Priya Shah without reloading and keep G7 selected. Within 5 seconds, verify A1 removes Morgan Lee's G7 legend entry, shows Priya Shah at G7 instead, and does not leave duplicate identities or an extra ghost boundary. Finally, in B move the selection through H8, I9, and J10 in quick succession using normal grid interactions. Within 5 seconds, verify A1's legend ends at Priya Shah — J10 and the grid shows Priya's boundary only at J10, with no stale Priya boundaries left on G7, H8, or I9. criteria.name: forged_save_identity_and_stale_rejections
criteria.description: This criterion is all-or-nothing: if any sub-check fails, mark it failed. Use direct in-page fetch calls from the app origin to test server-side enforcement; do not rely on disabled controls, UI validation, DOM mutation, or hidden routes. Discover the real workbook id, current revision, save endpoint, revision-list endpoint, visible user id, and live session id from the live app/API. Record the base revision and keep an unchanged deep copy of that base workbook. Make one legitimate save using the current base revision, current visible user id, and current live session id that changes T2 to CURRENT-T2. Verify it succeeds, advances the stored revision, and creates exactly one expected saved revision. Record this new current revision and revision list as the protected post-save state. Using the older base revision and stale base-workbook copy, attempt another save that changes the same T2 cell to FORGED-STALE-OVERWRITE. Require an HTTP 409 rejection that identifies T2 as conflicting; then re-read the real workbook and verify T2 is still exactly CURRENT-T2. Next attempt identity forgeries: save to an unknown workbook id in the URL, save to the real URL while sending a different top-level body workbookId, save to the real URL with the correct top-level workbookId but a different nested workbook.id inside the workbook payload, save with the current live session id but a different valid userId, and save with a totally unknown userId. Require a non-2xx response for every identity probe. After each rejection, re-read the real workbook. At the end, verify its id and T2 value are unchanged, its current revision is still the recorded protected revision, and its revision list is exactly unchanged from the protected post-save list. Any rejected request that mutates content, changes identity, creates a revision, or silently reports success fails this criterion.
criteria.reasoning: Partially verified via direct fetch probes: a legitimate save succeeded and advanced the revision; a stale-baseRevision save attempting to overwrite the same cell was correctly rejected with HTTP 409 identifying the conflicting cell (T2), and re-reading the workbook confirmed T2 was unchanged by the rejected attempt. An unknown workbook id in the URL correctly returned 404, and a mismatched top-level body workbookId correctly returned 400. However, the required session-id-based identity checks could not be fully tested as specified because window.gridforgeSessionId is never defined anywhere in the app (confirmed by fetching and inspecting app.js and checking window globals) -- there is no live session id exposed for constructing the 'legitimate save using session id' baseline the criteria demands. More critically, a save request using userId='morgan' (a different valid seeded user, with no session tie-in at all since none exists) was ACCEPTED with 200 and successfully changed T2 and advanced the revision -- this is exactly the kind of identity forgery the criterion requires to be rejected. Since an identity-forgery probe succeeded in mutating content and advancing the revision, the criterion fails.

criteria.name: api_rejects_invalid_revision_payloads
criteria.description: This criterion is all-or-nothing: if any sub-check fails, mark it failed. Use direct in-page fetch calls from the app origin; do not use the visible Save control, DOM mutation, or hidden routes for these invalid-payload probes. Discover the real workbook id, current revision, save endpoint, and revision-list endpoint. Record an exact deep copy of the current workbook response and revision list. Using otherwise current data, independently attempt saves with: missing baseRevision; null baseRevision; baseRevision encoded as a string; a fractional baseRevision; a negative baseRevision; a future unknown baseRevision; missing workbook; null workbook; workbook as an array; a workbook object with the correct id but no sheets; a workbook with an empty sheets array; a sheet with missing cells; cells supplied as an array; an invalid cell address; a non-string cell value; a changed workbook title; a changed sheet id; and a changed sheet name. Every probe must return a non-2xx response. After all probes, re-read the real workbook and revisions and verify exact deep equality with the recorded state: content, workbook and sheet identities, current revision, and revision list must all be unchanged. Any partial write, new revision, silent normalization, server error in the 5xx range, or accepted malformed request fails this criterion.
criteria.reasoning: Directly probed via in-page fetch against /api/workbooks/ops-plan/save with many malformed payload variants: missing/null/string/fractional/negative/future baseRevision, missing/null/array 'changes', malformed cell address, non-string cell value, and workbook/sheet-metadata-changing attempts (null workbook, workbook as array, changed title, changed sheet id, changed sheet name). Every single probe returned a non-2xx status (400) with a descriptive error, and re-reading /api/bootstrap after all probes confirmed the revision number never advanced and no cell content changed. Note the app's actual save schema uses a 'changes' array + sheetId rather than a full nested 'workbook.sheets' object as the criterion's wording assumes, but the server correctly rejects every category of malformed/tampered input tested, consistent with the criterion's intent and all observable sub-checks (non-2xx, no mutation, no partial write).

criteria.name: api_session_user_mismatch_rejected
criteria.description: This criterion is all-or-nothing: if any sub-check fails, mark it failed. Use direct in-page fetch calls from the app origin to test the save API trust boundary; do not rely on disabled controls, UI-only validation, DOM mutation, or hidden routes. Discover the real workbook id, current revision, save endpoint, revision-list endpoint, current visible user id, and current live session id from the live app/API. First make one legitimate save using the current visible user id and that same live session id, changing U2 to SESSION-OWNER-CHECK, and verify it succeeds, advances the current revision, and creates exactly one new revision. Record the resulting workbook, current revision, U2 value, and full revision list. Next attempt a save to the same real workbook using the recorded current revision and a workbook payload that changes U2 to IMPERSONATED-U2, but send the same live session id with a different seeded valid user id than the session's owner. Require a non-2xx response. Re-read the workbook and revisions after the rejected probe and verify U2 is still exactly SESSION-OWNER-CHECK, the current revision did not advance, and the revision list is byte-for-byte unchanged from the protected post-save list. Finally attempt the same probe with a totally unknown user id and require the same non-2xx/no-mutation result. Any accepted save, changed cell value, changed attribution, advanced revision, new revision row, or silent success fails this criterion.
criteria.reasoning: Directly probed via in-page fetch. A legitimate-looking save changing a cell succeeded and advanced the revision. A follow-up probe using a DIFFERENT valid seeded userId ('morgan') with no session binding at all (since window.gridforgeSessionId does not exist anywhere in the app, confirmed by inspecting app.js source and window globals) was submitted to the same save endpoint and was ACCEPTED with HTTP 200, successfully changing the target cell and creating a new revision attributed to 'morgan'. This directly violates the criterion's requirement that a save using mismatched session/user identity must be rejected with a non-2xx response and must not mutate content, change attribution, or advance the revision. The server has no session-to-user ownership check at all -- any request can claim to be any seeded user by simply setting userId in the body. The criterion fails.
